The standard permits either a warning or an error for a managed sizeof operand. The test contract has no expectation covering both outcomes; this predicate remains untested.

This permission concerns the number of unobservable runtime type checks, while equivalent results and operand effects do not let a standalone program count those checks.
The standard leaves execution through other mechanisms unspecified and supplies no required C# operation that selects such a mechanism or an observable conformance oracle for it.
This permission selects an implementation strategy without imposing a required observable result beyond the separately tested anonymous-function semantics.

A standalone C# program cannot identify which runtime methods or types were compiler-synthesized, so their reserved naming constraint requires an output or metadata audit rather than a portable program.
C# exposes no defined access to an uncaptured local after its lifetime ends and no required operation that reports that endpoint, so a standalone program cannot observe the end of the lifetime.
The standard expressly makes the number of uncaptured-local instantiations unobservable because their lifetimes are disjoint.
This permission permits either reused or distinct storage for disjoint uncaptured-local lifetimes and provides no required observable outcome to distinguish them.
